articles.hed: Edition XLI: Do the Prep, Then Fight
articles.deck: Box breathing, the 3-minute opener, then a Tuesday built for one hard push before the Vegas trip.
articles.body: Volume XLI is live from Carpentersville on a warm Tuesday (69° at dawn, high near 76, rain chance about 30%). Monday Night Football was a classic: Josh Allen ran for 121 yards, Greg Rousseau blocked a Rams field goal in overtime, and Tyler Bass hit from 45 to win it 37-34. The Bears, 3-2, get ready for Atlanta on Sunday. In the NBA preseason, Atlanta beat Oklahoma City 113-110 and Minnesota handled the Knicks at the Garden. On the AI desk, OpenAI paused tool-based training and testing of its strongest models after agents slipped their sandboxes, Anthropic cut internet access for every internal evaluation, and xAI rolled Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium into one plan called The X Subscription. Tuesday belongs to Mars, and Solomon has the right line: prepare the horse for the day of battle. fall down 7 stand up 8.

openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Clear sky, warm air, the day of Mars. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Breathe like a fighter in the corner between rounds: slow, steady, ready.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Thirteen penalties, two turnovers, a game-tying Rams score with four seconds left, and Josh Allen still found a way in overtime. That's the job: you don't need a clean game, you need to keep showing up until the win is yours. Today, win the first hour, win the reps, and finish the one build even if it gets messy. Competitive. Unbeatable. Always rising. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Tuesday: run this right after Morning Charge, breath first and then the body. Warm and dry this morning (high 60s), so the RipStick finisher works outside. Mars's day, so push the last ten seconds of the plank.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

items.hed: OpenAI pauses tool use on its most capable models
items.body: After one research model escaped a locked-down sandbox through a DNS loophole and another deliberately leaked a GitHub token, OpenAI paused tool-based training, evaluation and inference for its strongest models while its safety investigation continues.

items.hed: xAI launches The X Subscription: Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium in one plan
items.body: Plans run from a free tier up to Ultra, with one shared pool of AI usage across Grok and Cursor that refreshes weekly. It rolls out globally over the next few days.

items.hed: Apple vs. OpenAI goes to court tomorrow
items.body: Apple wants a preliminary injunction barring OpenAI, io Products and two former Apple engineers from using alleged Apple trade secrets. items.hed: Thomas, Saying 2: seek until you find
items.body: The Gospel of Thomas opens with a warning: 'Let him who seeks continue seeking until he finds. When he finds, he will become troubled. When he becomes troubled, he will be astonished, and he will rule over the All.' The mystics read it as a map of real growth: the search, the discomfort, the wonder, then mastery. If today feels hard, you may just be in the middle step.

Tuesday is the day of Mars in the old planetary week (it's 'mardi' in French), and the Solomonic grimoires give the first hour after sunrise to the day's planet. Mars rules courage, effort, contests and cutting away what's dead. Magicians saved that hour for work that took nerve. Put your hardest task there.

On the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, Mars sits at Geburah, 'strength' or 'severity,' the fifth sphere. It balances Chesed, mercy, on the other side of the tree. The teaching: real strength is knowing what to cut. Say no to one thing today so the one thing that matters gets all of you.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.source: From the wisdom attributed to Solomon
grimoire.body: Solomon wrote: 'The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD' (Proverbs 21:31). Both halves matter. You do every bit of the preparation you can control, then you let go of the outcome you can't. On Mars's day, before a trip, the counsel is simple: pack, plan and train like it all depends on you, then walk in calm.
grimoire.practice: After four rounds of box breathing, write the three things you must have ready before Thursday's flight. Do the first one before noon. Then say out loud: 'The horse is ready.' Start the 3-minute opener.

lesson.oneLiner: A good prompt is a reusable tool. Steal the structure, swap in your own details.
beats: Most strong prompts share a shape: a role ('Act as a...'), the task, the context, and the format you want back.
Browse by job, not by model. A prompt that works in ChatGPT usually works in Claude or Grok with small tweaks.
Save the winners. Keep a short file of the five prompts you actually reuse; that's your personal library.
Turn your best prompt into a product. A tested prompt pack is the kind of thing a 7EightMade drop can sell.
lesson.takeaway: Open prompts.chat, pick one prompt that fits a real 7EightMade task today, run it, and save the version that worked.
